memory_candidates.content: `git commit -- <pathspec>` is NOT equivalent to committing only what's staged for that path -- it auto-includes CURRENT WORKING-TREE changes for any named path, regardless of index state. If you use `git apply --cached <patch>` to stage only some hunks of a file (to avoid sweeping in an unrelated concurrent task's uncommitted edit to the same file), a subsequent `git commit -m ... -- <path>` will silently re-absorb the unstaged working-tree hunks too. The safe pattern: stage exactly what you want with `git add`/`git apply --cached`, then commit with a BARE `git commit -m ...` (no trailing pathspec) so only the index content is committed.

When a shared JSON ledger/index file (e.g. index-entries.json) already carries an unrelated uncommitted stray edit from a different in-flight task before your own edit begins, isolate your commit to only your own hunks via a hand-crafted patch applied with `git apply --cached`, rather than whole-file `git add` via a generic scoped-commit helper. Cross-check `specs/state.json` for any task with status `implementing`/`researching` whose file_scope or description names the same file before assuming a stray working-tree diff is safe to sweep into your commit.
